 Anthony Davis 
 WAS 
 Forward-Center 
 #23 
 Player Stats
 Link copied to clipboard! 
 Anthony Davis recorded a double-double on Thursday with 30 points (13-of-21 FGs), 15 rebounds, four assists and one steal against the Pistons.
 Though he ended up fouling out early in the second overtime, AD still had more than enough time to make his impact felt in this game. This was his fourth straight game with at least 20 points and 10 rebounds, though he was able to set a new season high for boards in this one. Though AD will always have his question marks, he’s one of the most dominant players in fantasy basketball when he’s on the court. He’ll look to stay hot against the Rockets to wrap up the week on Sunday.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Anthony Davis put up 21 points (7-of-20 FGs, 7-of-9 FTs), 13 rebounds, and two blocks on Wednesday against the Pacers. 
 Davis wasn’t as efficient in this one which impacted his stat line, but overall, a very solid game. It’s hard to complain with a double-double with some blocks. As always, the value with AD is going to be lower than the production in trades due to the reputation with the injuries. If you’re looking to trade AD, finding similar value to what he’s doing now would be ideal. 
 Anthony Davis 
 WAS 
 Forward-Center 
 #23 
 Anthony Davis erupted for a season-high 44 points (16-of-21 FGs, 10-of-11 FTs), 13 rebounds, one assist and one steal over 34 minutes as the Wizards fell to the Pistons 122-111 on Monday. 
 Davis was nearly unstoppable in the opening half, connecting on 10-of-11 shots from the floor and all eight of his nine free-throw attempts to pour in a staggering 30 points. It was the highest-scoring first half by any player in the league this season, surpassing Victor Wembanyama’s 29-point outburst earlier this month. He accounted for more than half of Washington’s 58 first-half points in his return from a three-game absence due to a sprained ankle. Clearly, he’s feeling fine from a physical standpoint. Unfortunately, it wasn’t enough to power the Wizards to a win as they committed a staggering 18 turnovers in a losing effort.

 Anthony Davis took advantage of the Hawks’ size with 26 points (12-of-19 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), 10 rebounds, three assists and three blocks in a loss. 
 He did tweak his ankle in the first quarter which will be something to monitor if it flares up but it didn’t impact him much in this game. He took advantage of his size over the Hawk’s smaller big men and had a good game. The next game the Wizards play is against the Hawks in Atlanta, so if he’s healthy, it’s possible that he has a similar performance against them on Friday.

 Zaccharie Risacher delivered 18 points (8-of-9 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs) and five rebounds over 27 minutes in Sunday’s blowout loss to the Celtics.
 Risacher was one of the few bright spots on an otherwise forgettable affair in Boston, as he saw huge minutes off the bench in a lopsided affair and was nearly perfect from the floor. His lone miss came from three-point range where he finished 1-of-2. The former top-overall pick from the 2024 NBA Draft fell out of favor in Atlanta, but he’s still young enough to envision a scenario where the change of scenery helps him turn things around. This effort certainly qualifies as a step in the right direction.

 Coming off a game in which he scored 27 points in a loss to the Rockets, George struggled on Sunday.  Darryn Peterson recorded 17 points (7-of-20 FGs), five rebounds, four assists, one steal, one block and three three-pointers in Sunday’s loss to the Spurs.
 Shooting the ball efficiently was an issue for all Jazz starters except Mo Bamba, who went 10-of-13, so Peterson wasn’t alone in his struggles. Plus, San Antonio’s athletic backcourt isn’t easy to deal with, especially for a rookie guard. The good news for fantasy managers was that Peterson posted solid numbers in rebounds and assists and kept the turnovers in check. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Mo Bamba accounted for 26 points (10-of-13 FGs, 0-of-3 FTs), five rebounds, four assists, two steals, one block and six three-pointers in Sunday’s loss to the Spurs.
 With Jaxson Hayes joining the list of injured Jazz big men, Bamba was inserted into the starting lineup on Sunday. He made the most of his opportunity, having one of the best games of his NBA career. Shockingly, Bamba went 6-of-6 from beyond the arc and recorded a full stat line. The Jazz play four games next week, starting with the Clippers on Tuesday. If they remain this shorthanded, Bamba’s worth a roll of the dice in deep leagues. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Dylan Harper finished Sunday’s win over the Jazz with 31 points (12-of-23 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), nine rebounds, four assists, one steal and two three-pointers.
 After scoring 19 points or fewer in five straight and six of San Antonio’s first seven games of November, Harper had one of the best games of his young NBA career on Sunday. The second-year guard recorded his first 30-point game as a pro while finishing one rebound shy of a double-double. Harper has been a reliable fantasy option this season, and De’Aaron Fox (hip) not playing on Sunday raised his ceiling.

 Stephon Castle recorded 20 points (6-of-11 FGs, 8-of-9 FTs), four rebounds, nine assists and four steals in Sunday’s win over the Jazz.
 Castle’s windmill dunk with 47.4 seconds left in the fourth quarter extended the Spurs’ lead to six and essentially ended the game. The third-year guard had an excellent night, shooting high percentages from the field and the foul line and dishing out nine assists. The Spurs didn’t have De’Aaron Fox, which gave Castle and Dylan Harper more room to make plays, and they were both excellent against the Jazz.

 Victor Wembanyama tallied 26 points (10-of-21 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), 11 rebounds, six assists, one steal, five blocks and four three-pointers in Sunday’s win over the Jazz.
 In addition to recording his 10th double-double of the season, Wembanyama finished Sunday’s victory with five blocks. He’s rejected at least five shots in seven of his first 14 games. Wembanyama and the Spurs play three games next week, starting with the Pistons on Tuesday. While it would be nice for fantasy managers to get four games out of Wemby, that isn’t a big deal given his productivity.
